changes: Removed Rāmakṛṣṇa (p6) as scribe: 'śrīrāmakṛṣṇaḥ subham astu' is most naturally a closing invocation, not a scribe's name; the wrote_for relation went with it

Devadatta: roles changed from owner to scribe + owner. The construction (descent chain, then the name, then 'pustakaṃ liṣitaṃ') presents him as the writer, which matches the catalogue. Confidence lowered to medium
Pyākurala (Pyākurel, a Nepali Brahmin surname) moved into Devadatta's titles/affiliation and removed from as_written

The descent chain is now read as 'X's descendant's son' at each step (prapautra-suta, pautra-suta, putra-suta, suta). This keeps the same five-generation line (Sadāśiva → Śrīkānta → Bālakṛṣṇa → Harikṛṣṇa → Devadatta) but explains the kin terms consistently. Evidence strings updated
Sadāśiva: the 'śarman' title is uncertain because 'savarṇa' is corrupt; confidence set to medium
Notes updated about the date discrepancy and the reading of the name

notes: The two dates disagree. Śaka 1854 is about 1932 CE and corresponds to VS 1989. VS 1986 is about 1929/30 CE and corresponds to Śaka 1851. I recorded the VS date. The descent chain is garbled ('prapautrāyaḥ suta', 'prauyaḥ suta', 'putrāyaḥ sutaḥ', 'putrāyaḥ suteḥ'). I read it as Devadatta being the great-great-grandson of Sadāśiva, great-grandson of Śrīkānta, grandson of Bālakṛṣṇa and son of Harikṛṣṇa, which gives a single line of descent. 'devadattapādhyā pyākuralapustakaṃ liṣitaṃ' means Devadatta Upādhyāya Pyākurel either wrote the book (as the catalogue says) or owned it ('Pyākurel's book'). I gave him both roles. 'śrīrāmakṛṣṇaḥ' just before 'subham astu' is most likely an invocation. It could possibly be a separate scribe, but that is unlikely. 'sadāśivasavarṇa' is corrupt; it may stand for 'sadāśivaśarmaṇa'. 'gograsya' should read 'gotrasya'.
